points: A group of elders comes to Yechezkel planning to twist his words: ask questions, then misquote him as permitting idolatry mixed into Jewish practice, and use his authority to lead the people astray.
Hashem punishes this plan even as a thought. Normally a person is not punished for an aveira they only intended, but idolatry is the exception, because it leads the Jewish people astray.
Misrepresenting great people to borrow their authority is nothing new. People have been turning to gedolim and distorting what they really hold for some 2,500 years.

Even if Noach, Iyov and Daniel lived in that generation, they could save only themselves. All three lived through dark times without saving others, so the people could not rely on the mere presence of tzaddikim to rescue everyone.

The survivors of Yerushalayim's destruction will bring comfort: they will admit the prophets were right and they were wrong. Understanding why suffering came, and recognizing Hashem's hand even in punishment, gives comfort and direction for rebuilding in exile.
